newsitem.title: UK: Pharmacia & Upjohn abandons MS trials.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia & Upjohn abandons MS trials.

text.p: Swedish-U.S drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc said on Wednesday it had abandoned late-stage clinical trials of a treatment for multiple sclerosis because of "an unexpected incidence" of heart attacks.

In a statement the company said trials of Linomide Tablets, also known as Roquinimex, had been stopped after eight cases of heart attacks were reported in two Phase III trials to evaluate the drug's safety and efficacy. No heart attacks were reported from a third trial.
The company had been hoping to file Linomide for regulatory approval in Europe and the U.S. in 2000 according to its recently-published 1996 annual report.

The two studies in which the problems occurred began enrolling patients in April 1996 and included 1,200 people in North America, Europe and Australia. Pharmacia & Upjohn said treatment with Linomide would be stopped for patients in all three trials.
"The company has determined that the occurrence of these events produces an unacceptable benefit-risk profile for Linomide in this particular indication," the statement said.

Linomide was being evaluated in the two most common forms of MS, which affect about 90 percent of all sufferers. The disease results in progressive loss of control over bodily movements. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
